# References, glossary, and annotations {short-title="References"}

This chapter presents the bibliographic citation system (IEEE style via
`IEEEtran-francais.bst`), the glossary and acronym system, collaborative comments,
and special front matter pages.

## Bibliographic citations {#sec-citations}

### Basic syntax

Citations are inserted with `[@key]`. The key corresponds to the BibTeX identifier
defined in `references.bib`:

````markdown
Computer typesetting was revolutionised by Knuth [@Knuth1984],
whose \TeX{} system was made accessible by Lamport with \LaTeX{} [@Lamport1994].
Quarto [@Allaire2022] unifies these tools in a modern publishing environment.
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:** Computer typesetting was revolutionised by Knuth
[@Knuth1984], whose \TeX{} system was made accessible by Lamport with \LaTeX{}
[@Lamport1994]. Quarto [@Allaire2022] unifies these tools in a modern publishing
environment.
:::

### Multiple references

````markdown
Python visualisation tools [@Hunter2007] and typographic reference works
[@Bringhurst2004; @Mittelbach2023] complement the author's toolkit.
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:** Python visualisation tools [@Hunter2007] and typographic reference works
[@Bringhurst2004; @Mittelbach2023] complement the author's toolkit.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Always use `[@key]` with brackets

The `IEEEtran-francais.bst` style uses `natbib`. The `@key` syntax without brackets
calls `\citet{}` which is broken with IEEEtran — it produces the author name followed
by `[?]`. **Always use `[@key]`** to obtain `[N]` (IEEE numbering).
:::

### The `references.bib` file

The `references.bib` file must be located **at the project root**. Pandoc in natbib
mode generates `\bibliography{references}` (without a path), and BibTeX looks for the
file in the current directory. A file in `content_en/references.bib` will not be
found.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Bibliography managers

Zotero (with the Better BibTeX connector), JabRef, or Mendeley export directly to
`.bib` format. The `@IEEEtranBSTCTL` entry at the top of the file configures the
IEEEtran style (number of authors before "et al.", etc.) — do not remove it.
:::

## Glossary and acronyms {#sec-glossary}

### Declaring entries in `glossaire-entries.qmd`

All entries are declared in
`content_en/frontmatter/glossaire-entries.qmd` via two shortcodes:

````markdown
{{</* acr label ABBREV "Full expansion" */>}}
{{</* terme label "word" "Complete definition of the term" */>}}
````

The shortcodes automatically write `_glossaire-entries.tex` (read by LaTeX) and
populate the HTML tables. Labels must be unique.

### Using acronyms in the text

Four shortcodes allow referencing an acronym in the desired form:

| Shortcode | PDF output | HTML output |
|:----------|:-----------|:------------|
| `{{</* gls cnam */>}}` | short form (1st use: long) | short form |
| `{{</* acrs cnam */>}}` | always short form | always short form |
| `{{</* acrl cnam */>}}` | always long form | always long form |
| `{{</* acrf cnam */>}}` | long (short) | long (short) |

: Glossary reference shortcodes. {#tbl-gloss-shortcuts}

Examples in context:

````markdown
The {{</* acrs cnam */>}} ({{</* acrl cnam */>}}) was founded in 1794.
The {{</* acrf qmd */>}} format is Quarto's native format.
The {{< acrf toc >}} is generated automatically by Quarto.
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:** The {{< acrs cnam >}} ({{< acrl cnam >}}) was founded in 1794. The
{{< acrf qmd >}} format is Quarto's native format.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## PDF vs HTML behaviour

In PDF, `{{< gls label >}}` expands on the first occurrence (long form + abbreviation
in parentheses) then uses the short form. In HTML, this first-occurrence logic is not
handled by the shortcode — it always produces the short form. For consistency, prefer
`{{< acrf label >}}` on the first occurrence in the text, and `{{< acrs label >}}`
thereafter.
:::

## Collaborative comments (`quarto-comments`) {#sec-comments}

### Configuration in `_quarto.yml`

The `quarto-comments` extension (folder `_extensions/comments/`) is configured via
the `comments:` key in `_quarto.yml`:

````yaml
comments:
  enabled: true
  show_author: true
  authors:
    author:
      name: "Eric Bavu"
      color_html: "#005EA5"
      color_latex: "blue!20"
    supervisor:
      name: "Abbé Grégoire"
      color_html: "#D55E00"
      color_latex: "orange!30"
````

### The four comment types

````markdown
{{</* comment "Rephrase this sentence, it is too long." author="supervisor" */>}}
{{</* todo "Add a figure illustrating this point." author="author" */>}}
{{</* note "See also Bringhurst 2004, §2.4." author="supervisor" */>}}
{{</* question "Is this result reproducible on another dataset?" author="supervisor" inline=true */>}}
````

Rendered in context — here is a sentence with a margin annotation
{{< comment "This is a 'comment' type annotation by the supervisor." author="dir" >}}
and a task to complete:

{{< todo "Replace this example with a real experimental result before the defence." author="auteur" >}}

A bibliographic note {{< note "See Knuth 1984, chapter 12." author="dir" inline=true >}} inline.

::: {.callout-important}
## Disable comments before final submission

Before submitting the thesis to the doctoral school and depositing it on theses.fr,
set `comments: enabled: false` in `_quarto.yml`. Annotations must not appear in the
official archived version.
:::

## Special front matter pages {#sec-frontmatter}

### Résumé and abstract

The `resume.qmd` and `abstract.qmd` pages use CSS classes that add a left border in
HTML:

````markdown
::: {.resume-block}
Text of the résumé in French.

**Mots-clés :** mot1, mot2, mot3
:::
````

::: {.callout-important}
## French résumé mandatory for all Cnam theses

Even for a thesis written in English, a French résumé is **mandatory** according to
the {{< acrs abes >}} rules for deposit on theses.fr. This is the role of the file
`content_en/frontmatter/resume.qmd` in the English profile.
:::

### The Individual Monitoring Committee ({{< acrs csi >}})

::: {.callout-note}
## French doctoral process — the {{< acrs csi >}}

The {{< acrf csi >}} has been mandatory since 2016 for all doctoral students in
France. It meets at least once a year, independently of the thesis supervisor, to
verify progress, working conditions, and adherence to the schedule. The minutes of
the {{< acrs csi >}} meeting must be included in the defence dossier.

The HTML version of this thesis template is particularly well suited for {{< acrs csi >}}
meetings: it allows sharing a link to the online version, which is easier to navigate
than a 200-page PDF.
:::
